Geographic focus:

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — covers the ongoing Yemen civil war since 2014 and recent clashes
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Houthi offensive trajectory, potential capture of Red Sea coastal positions, naval blockade implications
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — prolonged disruption of Bab al-Mandeb, compounded by Strait of Hormuz closure since March 2026

Synopsis:
Intensifying ground combat between Houthi forces and Saudi-backed Yemeni government troops is escalating along Yemen's western coast, with Houthis targeting strategic positions overlooking Bab al-Mandeb strait. The article situates this within a broader maritime disruption context: Bab al-Mandeb carries ~10% of global trade toward the Suez Canal, and the Strait of Hormuz has been virtually closed since March 2026. A Houthi naval blockade against Saudi Arabia is already active. If Houthis secure key coastal positions, their ability to disrupt Red Sea shipping materially increases, with direct knock-on effects on global energy and goods supply chains.
